method: Independent offline reading of acquired original text and maps, full selected source/baseline geometry and raw-byte hashes; independent binary decode plus production-decoder replay. Historical names are leads only.

prominent_geometry_warning.result: Substantial visible land overreach and incomplete upstream detail prevent accepting this polygon as an accurate Três Irmãos water mask.

findings.approved_name_scope: Chinese government-published usage and English scientific usage identify the generalized whole lake. This is research support, not product-field approval.
limits: All 95 ordered coordinates were checked. The broad west basin, northwest apex, indented north shore, concave south shore and southeast-curving arm match the named full-lake inset.
Frontiers Figure 1 partly obscures the shore with labels/tracks and does not establish shoreline date, CRS or independent geometry lineage; the match is not an independent survey.
The NIGLAS map distinguishes the northern upstream lakes; overflow connectivity does not merge their names into this polygon.
Chinese aliases are source-reported usage. Tibetan script, Korean name, legal naming act and effective date remain unestablished.

findings.identity: Três Irmãos reservoir, lower Rio Tietê
findings.approved_name_scope: Portuguese operator map form and ONS proper-name usage support the main reservoir association only. No scalar product field or whole-polygon water mask is approved.
limits: All 184 ordered coordinates were checked. The northwest–southeast main basin and lateral arms associate with the named reservoir, but broad polygon margins and southern projections contain visible mapped land.
The source eastern end truncates upstream detail toward Buritama. The overlay does not establish a precise dam, channel, tributary-mouth or adjoining-reservoir boundary.
Yellow lines on the operator map mark reforestation projects, not a certified water boundary. Land mismatch is assessed against underlying imagery as well as the full map context.
Assumed WGS84/UTM22S registration is diagnostic. Fit residuals are label-fit residuals, not shoreline error; no overlap or land fraction is measured.

Ilha Solteira and Jupiá remain separate Paraná installations; Nova Avanhandava and downstream Tietê/lock waters remain separately described. Exhaustive exclusion against adjacent vector polygons was not possible.

findings.approved_name_scope: English mapped usage identifies the full generalized Buffalo Lake basin; the Tathlina lead is excluded for this feature. No product name field is approved.
limits: All 88 ordered coordinates were checked. Federal sheet 85B labels the corresponding entire lake between 116°W and 115°W north of 60°N, including its west arm, enlarged northeast head and south-projecting lobe.
Two regional GNWT maps distinguish Buffalo east/southeast of Enterprise from Tathlina west of Enterprise near 117–118°W. The oil/gas map clips Buffalo and is not the full-perimeter source.
The 1975 federal thematic sheet uses older NAD27 base mapping. No datum transformation, quantitative registration or overlap calculation was performed.
The one-ring source is highly generalized; islands, small adjoining waters and exact seasonal shores are unverified. Current registry status and Indigenous-language names are unestablished.

publication_scope: Own factual extraction and validation only. Selected Natural Earth geometries have their separate rights record. Raw source PDFs, maps, HTML and derivative crops are excluded.
review_reproduction: Run validate-independent-review.py with the existing local geometry cache and historical-input root; pass the private local-source index to repeat original-source byte checks. Visual source interpretation remains a human-readable review, not an automated proof.
